entities.name: Carlo Domenico del Carretto
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Carlo Domenico del Carretto, known as the "Cardinal of Finale," was a prominent Italian cardinal, diplomat, and papal legate whose career spanned the tumultuous period of the Italian Wars and the early stages of the Reformation. Born into the powerful Del Carretto family, Marquises of Finale, his influence extended across Western Europe, particularly in France, Germany, and England, where he served as a key intermediary for the Holy See from the late 15th century until his death in Rome on August 25, 1514. His diplomatic acumen was critical in navigating the complex web of alliances and conflicts between the major European powers and the papacy.

Elevated to Archbishop of Cosenza in 1489, del Carretto quickly rose through the ecclesiastical ranks, becoming Governor of Rome in 1495 and a cardinal in 1503 under Pope Julius II. He undertook numerous sensitive diplomatic missions, most notably as legate to France in 1503 and 1507, and to the Holy Roman Empire and England in 1509. He played a central role in the negotiations leading to the League of Cambrai in 1508, a formidable anti-Venetian alliance involving Pope Julius II, Emperor Maximilian I, King Louis XII of France, and King Ferdinand II of Aragon. Although initially involved with the schismatic Council of Pisa in 1511, he swiftly reconciled with Julius II and became an active participant in the legitimate Fifth Lateran Council (1512–1517), reaffirming his loyalty to the Roman Pontiff.
